sentences.zh: =郭子儀=郭子儀，華州鄭縣人。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi was a native of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was a native of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父敬之，歷綏、渭、桂、壽、泗五州刺史，以子儀貴，贈太保，追封祁國公。

translations.literal: His father Jingzhi had served successively as prefect of Sui, Wei, Gui, Shou, and Si—the five prefectures—and because of Ziyi's eminence was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guo Jingzhi had served in turn as prefect of five prefectures—Sui, Wei, Gui, Shou, and Si—and when Ziyi rose to greatness, Jingzhi was posthumously made Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 子儀長六尺餘，體貌秀傑，始以武舉高等補左衛長史，累歷諸軍使。

translations.literal: Ziyi was over six feet tall, with a handsome and outstanding physique. He first entered service through the military examination with a high grade, was appointed Left Guard senior recorder, and successively held various army commissioner posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi stood more than six feet tall, with a striking and imposing bearing. He first entered service after placing high in the military examination, was appointed senior recorder of the Left Guard, and went on to hold a series of army commissioner posts.

sentences.zh: 天寶八載，於木剌山置橫塞軍及安北都護府，命子儀領其使，拜左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao, the Hengsai Army and the Anbei Protectorate were established at Mount Mula; Ziyi was ordered to command them as commissioner and was appointed general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 8 (749), the Hengsai Army and the Anbei Protectorate were established at Mount Mula; Ziyi was placed in command as commissioner and appointed general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 十三載，移橫塞軍及安北都護府於永清柵北築城，仍改橫塞為天德軍，子儀為之使，兼九原太守、朔方節度右兵馬使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Hengsai Army and the Anbei Protectorate were moved north of Yongqing Stockade to build a fort; Hengsai was renamed the Tiande Army, with Ziyi as its commissioner, concurrently serving as prefect of Jiuyuan and right army-and-horse commissioner of the Shuofang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 13 (754), the Hengsai Army and the Anbei Protectorate were relocated north of Yongqing Stockade and a fort was built; Hengsai was renamed the Tiande Army, with Ziyi as commissioner, while also serving as prefect of Jiuyuan and right army-and-horse commissioner under the Shuofang military governor.

sentences.zh: 十四載，安祿山反。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, An Lushan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 14 (755), An Lushan rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以子儀為衛尉卿，兼靈武郡太守，充朔方節度使，詔子儀以本軍東討。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Ziyi was made Minister of the Guard and concurrently Administrator of Lingwu Commandery, appointed military governor of Shuofang, and ordered to lead his army east to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Ziyi was appointed Minister of the Guard and concurrent administrator of Lingwu Commandery, made military governor of Shuofang, and ordered to march east with his army against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 遂舉兵出單於府，收靜邊軍，斬賊將周萬頃，傳首闕下。

translations.literal: He then raised his army out of the Chanyu Protectorate, recovered the Jingbian Army, beheaded the rebel general Zhou Wanqing, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched out from the Chanyu Protectorate, recovered the Jingbian Army, beheaded the rebel general Zhou Wanqing, and sent his head to the court.

sentences.zh: 祿山遣大同軍使高秀巖寇河曲，子儀擊敗之，進收雲中馬邑，開東陘，以功加御史大夫。

translations.literal: Lushan sent the Datong Army commissioner Gao Xiuyan to raid the Hequ region; Ziyi defeated him, advanced to recover Yunzhong and Mayi, opened the Eastern Pass, and for his merit was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan sent the Datong Army commissioner Gao Xiuyan to raid the Hequ region; Ziyi routed him, advanced to recover Yunzhong and Mayi, opened the Eastern Pass, and was promoted to Censor-in-Chief for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 十五載正月，賊將蔡希德陷常山郡，執顏杲卿，河北郡縣皆為賊守。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, the rebel general Cai Xide captured Changshan Commandery and seized Yan Gaoqing; all the commanderies and counties of Hebei were held by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianbao 15 (756), the rebel general Cai Xide took Changshan Commandery and captured Yan Gaoqing; throughout Hebei, commanderies and counties fell under rebel control.

sentences.zh: 二月，子儀與河東節度使李光弼率師下井陘，拔常山郡，破賊於九門，南攻趙郡，生擒賊四千，皆舍之，斬偽太守郭獻璆，獲兵仗數萬。

translations.literal: In the second month, Ziyi and the Hedong military governor Li Guangbi led their armies down through Jingxing Pass, recovered Changshan Commandery, defeated the rebels at Jiumen, attacked Zhao Commandery to the south, captured four thousand rebels alive and released them all, beheaded the false prefect Guo Xianqiu, and seized tens of thousands of weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Ziyi and Hedong military governor Li Guangbi led their forces through Jingxing Pass, retook Changshan Commandery, routed the rebels at Jiumen, and pushed south into Zhao Commandery. They took four thousand rebels alive and then released them, executed the puppet prefect Guo Xianqiu, and captured tens of thousands of weapons.

sentences.zh: 師還常山，賊將史思明以數萬人踵其後，我行亦行，我止亦止。

translations.literal: As the army returned to Changshan, the rebel general Shi Siming followed with tens of thousands of men: when we marched, they marched; when we halted, they halted.
translations.idiomatic: As the army withdrew to Changshan, the rebel general Shi Siming followed with tens of thousands of men, matching their every move—marching when they marched and halting when they halted.

sentences.zh: 子儀選驍騎五百更挑之，三日至行唐，賊疲乃退，我軍乘之，又敗於沙河。

translations.literal: Ziyi selected five hundred crack horsemen to harry them in relays; after three days they reached Xingtang, and when the rebels were exhausted they withdrew; our army pressed them and defeated them again at Shahe.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi picked five hundred elite horsemen to harass them in relays. After three days they reached Xingtang; when the rebels were worn down and pulled back, the imperial forces pressed the pursuit and routed them again at Shahe.

sentences.zh: 祿山聞思明敗，乃以精兵益之。

translations.literal: When Lushan heard that Siming had been defeated, he sent elite troops to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan learned of Siming's defeat, he sent elite troops to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 我軍至恆陽，賊亦隨至。

translations.literal: Our army reached Hengyang, and the rebels followed as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army reached Hengyang, the rebels came up right behind them.

sentences.zh: 子儀堅壁自固，賊來則守，賊去則追，晝揚其兵，夕襲其幕，賊人不及息。

translations.literal: Ziyi strengthened his walls and held firm: when the rebels came he defended, when they left he pursued; by day he displayed his troops, by night he raided their camps, and the rebels had no chance to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi fortified his position behind stout walls: when the rebels advanced he stood on the defense, when they withdrew he gave chase; by day he paraded his forces, by night he struck their camps, giving the enemy no respite.

sentences.zh: 數日，光弼議曰：「賊怠矣，可以戰。

translations.literal: After several days, Guangbi proposed: "The rebels are weary; we can give battle."
translations.idiomatic: After several days, Guangbi argued, "The rebels are worn down—we can fight them now."

sentences.zh: 」六月，子儀、光弼率僕固懷恩、渾釋之、陳回光等陣於嘉山，賊將史思明、蔡希德、尹子奇等亦結陣而至，一戰敗之，斬馘四萬級，生擒五千人，獲馬五千匹，思明露髪跣足奔於博陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Ziyi and Guangbi, leading Pugu Huai'en, Hun Jinzhi, Chen Huiguang, and others, drew up battle lines at Jiashan; the rebel generals Shi Siming, Cai Xide, Yin Ziqi, and others also formed ranks and came up. In a single battle they were defeated: forty thousand heads were cut off, five thousand men captured alive, five thousand horses taken, and Siming fled to Boling with hair loose and feet bare.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Ziyi and Guangbi, with Pugu Huai'en, Hun Jinzhi, Chen Huiguang, and others, formed battle lines at Jiashan. The rebel generals Shi Siming, Cai Xide, Yin Ziqi, and others did the same and advanced to meet them. One engagement broke the enemy: forty thousand were slain, five thousand taken alive, five thousand horses captured, and Siming fled to Boling with hair unbound and barefoot.

sentences.zh: 於是河北十餘郡皆斬賊守者以迎王師。

translations.literal: Thereupon more than ten commanderies in Hebei all beheaded the rebel garrison commanders to welcome the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon more than ten Hebei commanderies executed their rebel garrison commanders to welcome the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 子儀將北圖范陽，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Ziyi was about to march north against Fanyang, and the army's renown rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi prepared to march north against Fanyang, and the army's prestige soared.

sentences.zh: 是月，哥舒翰為賊所敗，潼關不守，玄宗幸蜀，肅宗幸靈武，子儀副使杜鴻漸為朔方留後，奏迎車駕。

translations.literal: That month, Geshu Han was defeated by the rebels, Tong Pass could not be held, Emperor Xuanzong went to Shu, and Emperor Suzong went to Lingwu; Ziyi's deputy Du Hongjian, as acting Shuofang commander, memorialized to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, Geshu Han was defeated by the rebels and Tong Pass fell. Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu while Emperor Suzong went to Lingwu. Ziyi's deputy Du Hongjian, serving as acting Shuofang commander, memorialized to welcome the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 七月，肅宗即位，以賊據兩京，方謀收復，詔子儀班師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Suzong ascended the throne; because the rebels held the two capitals, recovery was being planned, and Ziyi was ordered to withdraw his army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Suzong took the throne. With the rebels holding both capitals, the court turned to planning their recovery and ordered Ziyi to withdraw his army.

sentences.zh: 八月，子儀與李光弼率步騎五萬至自河北。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Ziyi and Li Guangbi arrived from Hebei leading fifty thousand infantry and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Ziyi and Li Guangbi arrived from Hebei at the head of fifty thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷初立，兵眾寡弱，雖得牧馬，軍容缺然。

translations.literal: At that time the court had only just been established; its forces were few and weak, and though horses could be pastured, military appearance was still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The court had only just been established; its forces were few and weak, and though horses could be raised, the army still lacked proper equipment and bearing.

sentences.zh: 及子儀、光弼全師赴行在，軍聲遂振，興復之勢，民有望焉。

translations.literal: When Ziyi and Guangbi brought their full armies to the temporary capital, military prestige was immediately revived, the momentum for restoration grew, and the people had hope.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi and Guangbi brought their full armies to the temporary capital, military morale revived at once, the tide of restoration gathered strength, and the people dared to hope again.

sentences.zh: 詔以子儀為兵部尚書、同中書門下平章事，依前靈州大都督府長史、朔方軍節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ziyi Minister of War and Associate Director of the Secretariat with the Chancellery, while retaining his former posts as chief administrator of the Lingzhou Metropolitan Area Command and military governor of the Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Ziyi Minister of War and a co-director of the Secretariat with the Chancellery, while he retained his posts as chief administrator of the Lingzhou metropolitan command and military governor of the Shuofang Army.

sentences.zh: 肅宗大閱六軍，南趨關輔，至彭原郡，宰相房琯請兵萬人，自為統帥以討賊，帝素重琯，許之。

translations.literal: Suzong reviewed the Six Armies on a grand scale and marched south toward the Guanzhong region, reaching Pengyuan Commandery. The chief minister Fang Guan requested ten thousand troops and asked to command them himself to attack the rebels; the emperor had long esteemed Fang and granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong held a grand review of the Six Armies and marched south toward Guanzhong, reaching Pengyuan Commandery. Chief minister Fang Guan asked for ten thousand men and offered to lead them personally against the rebels; the emperor had long held Fang in high regard and agreed.

sentences.zh: 兵及陳濤，為賊所敗，喪師殆盡。

translations.literal: When the army reached Chen Tao, it was defeated by the rebels and nearly wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Chen Tao, the rebels routed it and nearly annihilated the force.

sentences.zh: 方事討除，而軍半殪，唯倚朔方軍為根本。

translations.literal: Just as the campaign to suppress the rebels was underway, half the army was destroyed; only the Shuofang Army could be relied on as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the campaign to crush the rebellion was getting under way, half the army had been lost; only the Shuofang Army remained as the bedrock of imperial power.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賊將阿史那從禮以同羅、僕骨五千騎出塞，誘河曲九府、六胡州部落數萬，欲迫行在。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the rebel general Ashina Congli led five thousand Tongluo and Pugu horsemen out beyond the frontier, induced tens of thousands from the nine prefectures and six Hu prefectures of the Hequ region to join him, and intended to press upon the temporary capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the rebel general Ashina Congli led five thousand Tongluo and Pugu horsemen beyond the frontier, drew tens of thousands from the nine Hequ prefectures and the six Hu prefectures to his banner, and aimed to threaten the temporary capital.

sentences.zh: 子儀與回紇首領葛邏支往擊敗之，斬獲數萬，河曲平定。

translations.literal: Ziyi went with the Uyghur chief Eluozhi to attack and defeat them, killing and capturing tens of thousands, and the Hequ region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi marched with the Uyghur chief Eluozhi, defeated them, killed and captured tens of thousands, and pacified the Hequ region.

sentences.zh: 賊將崔乾祐守潼關。

translations.literal: The rebel general Cui Qianyou held Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Cui Qianyou held Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，子儀大破賊於潼關，崔乾祐退保蒲津。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, Ziyi inflicted a great defeat on the rebels at Tong Pass, and Cui Qianyou withdrew to defend Pujin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year, Ziyi routed the rebels at Tong Pass, and Cui Qianyou fell back to hold Pujin.

sentences.zh: 時永樂尉趙復、河東司戶韓旻、司士徐炅、宗子李藏鋒等，陷賊在蒲州，四人密謀俟王師至，則為內應。

translations.literal: At that time the Yongle district magistrate Zhao Fu, Hedong registrar Han Min, clerk Xu Jiong, and imperial clansman Li Cangfeng were trapped with the rebels in Pu Prefecture; the four secretly plotted that when the imperial army arrived they would act as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yongle district magistrate Zhao Fu, Hedong registrar Han Min, clerk Xu Jiong, and imperial clansman Li Cangfeng were trapped in rebel-held Pu Prefecture. The four secretly agreed to serve as inside collaborators once the imperial army arrived.

sentences.zh: 及子儀攻蒲州，趙復等斬賊守陴者，開門納子儀。

translations.literal: When Ziyi attacked Pu Prefecture, Zhao Fu and the others beheaded the rebel wall guards, opened the gates, and admitted Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi attacked Pu Prefecture, Zhao Fu and his companions killed the rebel guards on the walls, opened the gates, and welcomed Ziyi in.

sentences.zh: 乾祐與麾下數千人北走安邑，安邑百姓偽降，乾祐兵入將半，下懸門擊之，乾祐未入，遂得脫身東走。

translations.literal: Qianyou and several thousand of his followers fled north to Anyi; the people of Anyi feigned surrender, and when Qianyou's troops were halfway through the gate they dropped the portcullis and struck them. Qianyou did not enter and was able to escape eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyou fled north to Anyi with several thousand followers. The townspeople feigned surrender, and when his troops were halfway through the gate they dropped the portcullis and attacked. Qianyou never entered the city and escaped eastward.

sentences.zh: 子儀遂收陜郡永豐倉。

translations.literal: Ziyi then recovered the Yongfeng granary in Shaan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi then seized the Yongfeng granary in Shaan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 自是潼、陜之間無復寇鈔。

translations.literal: From then on there was no more rebel raiding between Tong and Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: From then on rebel raiders no longer troubled the region between Tong and Shaan.

sentences.zh: 是月，安祿山死，朝廷欲圖大舉，詔子儀還鳳翔。

translations.literal: That month An Lushan died; the court wished to mount a major campaign and ordered Ziyi back to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: That month An Lushan died. The court planned a major offensive and ordered Ziyi back to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 四月，進位司空，充關內、河東副元帥。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was promoted to Minister of Works and appointed deputy supreme commander of Guannei and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was promoted to Minister of Works and made deputy supreme commander for Guannei and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔子儀帥師趨京城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict ordered Ziyi to lead his army toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict ordered Ziyi to march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 師於潏水之西，與賊將安太清、安守忠戰，王師不利，其眾大潰，盡委兵仗於清渠之上。

translations.literal: The army fought west of the Wei River against the rebel generals An Taiqing and An Shouzhong; the imperial forces fared badly, their troops broke in great disorder, and they abandoned all weapons and armor along the Qing Canal.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Wei River his army met the rebel generals An Taiqing and An Shouzhong. The imperial forces were beaten, broke in disorder, and abandoned weapons and armor all along the Qing Canal.

sentences.zh: 子儀收合餘眾，保武功，詣闕請罪，乞降官資，乃降為左僕射，餘如故。

translations.literal: Ziyi gathered the survivors, held Wugong, went to court to confess fault, and begged to be reduced in rank; he was demoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs while his other posts remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi rallied the survivors, held Wugong, went to court to accept blame, and asked to be demoted. He was reduced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs while retaining his other offices.

sentences.zh: 九月，從元帥廣平王率蕃漢之師十五萬進收長安。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he followed the supreme commander, the Prince of Guangping, leading a mixed Tang and non-Han force of one hundred fifty thousand to advance and recover Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he followed supreme commander the Prince of Guangping, leading a combined force of one hundred fifty thousand Tang and allied troops to retake Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 回紇遣葉護太子領四千騎助國討賊，子儀與葉護宴狎修好，相與誓平國難，相得甚好。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs sent Crown Prince Yehu leading four thousand horsemen to aid the state against the rebels; Ziyi feasted and grew intimate with Yehu, and together they swore to end the national crisis, becoming very close.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs sent Crown Prince Yehu with four thousand horsemen to help the dynasty fight the rebels. Ziyi feasted with Yehu and won his friendship; they swore together to end the national crisis and became exceedingly close.

sentences.zh: 子儀奉元帥為中軍，與賊將安守忠、李歸仁戰於京西香積寺之北，王師結陣橫亙三十里，賊眾十萬陳於北。

translations.literal: Ziyi placed the supreme commander at the center of the army and fought the rebel generals An Shouzhong and Li Guiren north of Xiangji Temple west of the capital; the imperial army formed ranks stretching thirty li across, while one hundred thousand rebels deployed to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi placed the supreme commander at the center and fought the rebel generals An Shouzhong and Li Guiren north of Xiangji Temple west of the capital. The imperial army drew up a battle line thirty li wide, facing one hundred thousand rebels deployed to the north.

sentences.zh: 歸仁先薄我軍，我軍亂，李嗣業奮命馳突，擒賊十餘騎乃定。

translations.literal: Guiren first pressed our army; our ranks fell into disorder, but Li Siye charged desperately, captured more than ten rebel horsemen, and only then was order restored.
translations.idiomatic: Guiren struck first and threw the imperial line into disorder. Li Siye charged recklessly, seized more than ten rebel horsemen, and only then steadied the army.

sentences.zh: 回紇以奇兵出賊陣之後夾攻之，賊軍大潰，自午至酉，斬首六萬級。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs sent a surprise force around behind the rebel formation and attacked from both sides; the rebel army broke in great disorder, and from noon to dusk sixty thousand heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs sent a flanking force around the rear of the rebel line and attacked from both sides. The rebel army collapsed, and from noon to dusk sixty thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 賊將張通儒守長安，聞歸仁等敗，是夜奔陜郡。

translations.literal: The rebel general Zhang Tongru held Chang'an; hearing that Guiren and the others had been defeated, he fled that night to Shaan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Zhang Tongru held Chang'an. When he heard that Guiren and the others had been defeated, he fled that night to Shaan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 翌日，廣平王入京師，老幼百萬，夾道歡叫，涕泣而言曰：「不圖今日復見官軍。

translations.literal: The next day the Prince of Guangping entered the capital; a million old and young lined the roads cheering, weeping as they said: "We never expected to see the imperial army again today."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Prince of Guangping entered the capital. A million people young and old lined the streets, cheering and weeping as they cried, "We never dreamed we would see the imperial army again."

sentences.zh: 」廣平王休士三日，率師東趨。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping rested the troops for three days, then led the army eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The prince rested the troops for three days, then marched east.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在鳳翔聞捷，群臣稱賀，帝以宗廟被焚，悲咽不自勝，臣僚無不感泣。

translations.literal: Suzong at Fengxiang heard the victory; the ministers offered congratulations, but the emperor, because the ancestral temples had been burned, was overcome with grief and could not restrain himself, and the officials all wept in sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang, Suzong heard the news of victory. The ministers congratulated him, but the emperor, thinking of the burned ancestral temples, was overcome with grief, and the officials wept with him.

sentences.zh: 十月，安慶緒遣嚴莊悉其眾十萬來赴陜州，與張通儒同抗官軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, An Qingxu sent Yan Zhuang with his entire force of one hundred thousand to relieve Shaan Prefecture and, together with Zhang Tongru, resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month An Qingxu sent Yan Zhuang with his full force of one hundred thousand to relieve Shaan Prefecture and, with Zhang Tongru, oppose the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 賊聞官軍至，悉其眾屯於陜西，負山為陣。

translations.literal: When the rebels heard the imperial army had arrived, they massed all their troops west of Shaan and formed ranks with the mountain at their backs.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels heard the imperial army was coming, they gathered their full strength west of Shaan and formed battle lines with the mountain at their backs.

sentences.zh: 子儀以大軍擊其前，回紇登山乘其背，遇賊潛師於山中，與鬥過期，大軍稍卻。

translations.literal: Ziyi struck their front with the main army while the Uyghurs climbed the mountain and attacked from behind; they encountered a rebel ambush in the hills, fought past the appointed time, and the main army fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi struck their front with the main army while the Uyghurs climbed the mountain and hit them from behind. They ran into a rebel ambush in the hills, fought past the agreed time, and the main army gave ground slightly.

sentences.zh: 賊分兵三千人，絕我歸路，眾心大搖，子儀麾回紇令進，盡殺之。

translations.literal: The rebels detached three thousand men to cut off our line of retreat; morale shook greatly, but Ziyi ordered the Uyghurs forward and they killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent three thousand men to cut off the retreat. Morale wavered sharply, but Ziyi ordered the Uyghurs forward and they slaughtered them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 師馳至其後，於黃埃中發十餘箭，賊驚顧曰：「回紇來！

translations.literal: The army galloped to their rear; amid yellow dust more than ten arrows were loosed, and the rebels looked back in alarm, crying: "The Uyghurs are coming!"
translations.idiomatic: The army galloped around to their rear. More than ten arrows flew through the yellow dust, and the rebels looked back in alarm, shouting, "The Uyghurs are coming!"

sentences.zh: 」即時大敗，僵屍遍山澤。

translations.literal: At once they were utterly defeated, and corpses lay strewn across the hills and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: At once they were routed, and corpses covered the hills and marshes.

sentences.zh: 嚴莊、張通儒走歸洛陽，遂與安慶緒渡河保相州。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang and Zhang Tongru fled back to Luoyang, then crossed the river with An Qingxu to hold Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang and Zhang Tongru fled to Luoyang, then crossed the river with An Qingxu to hold Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子儀奉廣平王入東都，陳兵於天津橋南，士庶歡呼於路。

translations.literal: Ziyi escorted the Prince of Guangping into the Eastern Capital, arrayed troops south of Tianjin Bridge, and commoners and gentry cheered along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi escorted the Prince of Guangping into the Eastern Capital, drew up troops south of Tianjin Bridge, and people cheered all along the road.

sentences.zh: 偽侍中陳希烈、偽中書令張垍等三百餘人素服請罪，王慰撫遣之。

translations.literal: The false chief minister Chen Xilie, the false director of the Secretariat Zhang Ji, and more than three hundred others came in plain dress to plead guilty; the prince comforted them and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: The puppet chief minister Chen Xilie, puppet director of the Secretariat Zhang Ji, and more than three hundred others came in plain dress to plead guilty. The prince comforted them and let them go.

sentences.zh: 是時，河東、河西、河南賊所盜郡邑皆平，以功加司徒，封代國公，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: At that time the commanderies and districts seized by rebels in Hedong, Hexi, and Henan were all pacified; for his merit he was promoted to Minister of Education, enfeoffed as Duke of Dai, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: By then the rebel-held commanderies and districts of Hedong, Hexi, and Henan had all been recovered. For his achievements he was made Minister of Education, enfeoffed as Duke of Dai, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋入朝，天子遣兵仗戎容迎於灞上，肅宗勞之曰：「雖吾之家國，實由卿再造。

translations.literal: Soon he entered court; the Son of Heaven sent troops in martial array to welcome him at Bashang, and Suzong praised him, saying: "Though it is my house and state, in truth it was you who restored it."
translations.idiomatic: He soon came to court. The emperor sent troops in full martial array to welcome him at Bashang, and Suzong praised him: "Though this is my house and realm, in truth you restored it."

sentences.zh: 」子儀頓首感謝。

translations.literal: Ziyi bowed his head to the ground in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 十二月，還東都，命子儀經營北討。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he returned to the Eastern Capital and ordered Ziyi to organize the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he returned to the Eastern Capital and ordered Ziyi to organize the northern offensive.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年七月，破賊河上，擒偽將安守忠以獻，遂朝京師，敕百僚班迎於長樂驛，帝御望春樓待之，進位中書令。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Qianyuan, he defeated the rebels on the river, captured the false general An Shouzhong and presented him, then came to court at the capital; an edict ordered the hundred officials to line up and welcome him at Changle Post Station, the emperor waited for him atop Wangchun Tower, and he was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Qianyuan 1 (758), he defeated the rebels on the river, captured the puppet general An Shouzhong and presented him, then came to the capital. The hundred officials were ordered to line up and welcome him at Changle Post Station; the emperor waited atop Wangchun Tower and promoted him to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九月，奉詔大舉，子儀與河東節度使李光弼、關內節度使王思禮、北庭行營節度李嗣業、襄鄧節度使魯炅、荊南節度季廣琛、河南節度使崔光遠、滑濮節度許叔冀、平盧兵馬使董秦等九節度之師討安慶緒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, by imperial order a major campaign was launched: Ziyi, together with the armies of nine military governors—Hedong's Li Guangbi, Guannei's Wang Sili, Beiting field commander Li Siye, Xiang-Deng's Lu Jiong, Jingnan's Ji Guangchen, Henan's Cui Guangyuan, Hua-Pu's Xu Shuji, and Pinglu army commissioner Dong Qin—marched against An Qingxu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month a major campaign was ordered. Ziyi, with the armies of nine military governors—Li Guangbi of Hedong, Wang Sili of Guannei, Li Siye of the Beiting field command, Lu Jiong of Xiang-Deng, Ji Guangchen of Jingnan, Cui Guangyuan of Henan, Xu Shuji of Hua-Pu, and Dong Qin of Pinglu—marched against An Qingxu.

sentences.zh: 帝以子儀、光弼俱是元勛，難相統屬，故不立元帥。

translations.literal: Because both Ziyi and Guangbi were founding meritorious officials and difficult to place one under the other, no supreme commander was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Because both Ziyi and Guangbi were founding heroes and neither could readily command the other, no supreme commander was appointed.

sentences.zh: 唯以中官魚朝恩為觀軍容宣慰使。

translations.literal: Only the eunuch Yu Chao'en was made army-oversight commissioner and pacification envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Only the eunuch Yu Chao'en was made army-oversight commissioner and pacification envoy.

sentences.zh: 十月，子儀自杏園渡河，圍衛州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Ziyi crossed the river from Xingyuan and besieged Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Ziyi crossed the river from Xingyuan and besieged Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒與其驍將安雄俊、崔乾祐、薛嵩、田承嗣悉其眾來援，分為三軍。

translations.literal: An Qingxu, with his fierce generals An Xiongjun, Cui Qianyou, Xue Song, and Tian Chengsi, brought all their forces to relieve the city, dividing into three armies.
translations.idiomatic: An Qingxu marched to relieve the city with his crack generals An Xiongjun, Cui Qianyou, Xue Song, and Tian Chengsi at the head of their full forces, divided into three armies.

sentences.zh: 子儀陣以待之，預選射者三千人伏於壁內，誡之曰：「俟吾小卻，賊必爭進，則登城鼓噪，弓弩齊發以迫之。

translations.literal: Ziyi formed ranks to await them, beforehand selecting three thousand archers to lie in ambush within the walls, and instructed them: "When I feign a slight retreat, the rebels will surely press forward in rivalry; then mount the walls, beat drums and shout, and let bows and crossbows fire together to drive them back."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi drew up battle lines to meet them and beforehand picked three thousand archers to hide within the walls. He told them, "When I feign a slight retreat, the rebels will rush forward. Mount the walls, beat the drums, raise a clamor, and let bows and crossbows fire together to drive them back."

sentences.zh: 」既戰，子儀偽遁，賊果乘之，及壘門，遽聞鼓噪，俄而弓弩齊發，矢註如雨，賊徒震駭，子儀整眾追之，賊眾大敗。

translations.literal: When battle was joined, Ziyi feigned flight; the rebels indeed pursued, and when they reached the rampart gate they suddenly heard drums and shouts, and at once bows and crossbows fired together, arrows falling like rain. The rebels were terrified; Ziyi re-formed his troops and pursued, and the rebel army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, Ziyi feigned retreat. The rebels pursued as expected, and at the rampart gate drums and shouts erupted as bows and crossbows fired together, arrows falling like rain. The rebels were terrified. Ziyi re-formed his troops and pursued, routing the rebel army completely.

sentences.zh: 是役也，獲偽鄭王安慶和以獻，遂收衛州。

translations.literal: In this battle the false Prince of Zheng, An Qinghe, was captured and presented, and Weizhou was then recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle the puppet Prince of Zheng, An Qinghe, was captured and presented, and Weizhou was taken.

sentences.zh: 進軍趨鄴，與賊再戰於愁思岡，賊軍又敗，乃連營圍之。

translations.literal: The army advanced toward Ye, fought the rebels again at Chousi Ridge, defeated them once more, and then encamped in linked camps to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced on Ye, fought the rebels again at Chousi Ridge, routed them once more, and then laid siege with a chain of camps.

sentences.zh: 慶緒遣薛嵩以所乘馬十匹求救於史思明，且言禪代。

translations.literal: Qingxu sent Xue Song with ten of his own riding horses to beg Shi Siming for aid and to speak of abdicating the throne to him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu sent Xue Song with ten of his own horses to beg Shi Siming for help and to offer to abdicate in his favor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，思明遣將李歸仁率眾赴之，營於滏陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Siming sent the general Li Guiren with his troops to relieve them, encamping at Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Siming sent Li Guiren with his troops to relieve them and encamped at Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，史思明自率范陽精卒復陷魏州，乃偽稱燕王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Shi Siming personally led elite troops from Fanyang, recovered Weizhou, and declared himself false King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Shi Siming personally led elite Fanyang troops, retook Weizhou, and declared himself King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 王師雖眾，軍無統帥，進退無所承稟，自冬徂春，竟未破賊，但引漳水以灌其城，城中食盡，易子而食。

translations.literal: Though the imperial army was numerous, it had no commander-in-chief; advance and retreat had no authority to report to. From winter to spring they still had not broken the rebels, but only diverted the Zhang River to flood the city; inside the city food was exhausted and people exchanged children to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Though the imperial army was large, it had no commander-in-chief, and no one had authority over advance or retreat. From winter to spring they still failed to break the rebels, but only diverted the Zhang River to flood the city. Inside, food ran out and people resorted to exchanging children to eat.

sentences.zh: 二月，思明率眾自魏州來。

translations.literal: In the second month, Siming led his troops from Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Siming marched from Weizhou with his army.

sentences.zh: 李光弼、王思禮、許叔冀、魯炅前軍遇賊於鄴南，與之接戰，夷傷相半，魯炅中流矢。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi, Wang Sili, Xu Shuji, and Lu Jiong's vanguard met the rebels south of Ye and joined battle; casualties on both sides were about equal, and Lu Jiong was struck by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard of Li Guangbi, Wang Sili, Xu Shuji, and Lu Jiong met the rebels south of Ye and fought them to a bloody standstill. Lu Jiong was hit by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 子儀為後陣，未及合戰，大風遽起，吹沙拔木，天地晦暝，跬步不辯物色。

translations.literal: Ziyi was in the rear guard and had not yet joined battle when a great wind suddenly arose, blowing sand and uprooting trees; heaven and earth grew dark, and one could not distinguish objects a few steps away.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi held the rear and had not yet joined battle when a violent wind sprang up, whipping sand and uprooting trees until heaven and earth went dark and one could not see a few steps ahead.

sentences.zh: 我師潰而南，賊軍潰而北，委棄兵仗輜重，累積於路。

translations.literal: Our army broke southward and the rebel army broke northward, abandoning weapons and baggage piled along the road.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army broke southward and the rebel army broke northward, leaving weapons and baggage heaped along the road.

sentences.zh: 諸軍各還本鎮。

translations.literal: Each army returned to its home command.
translations.idiomatic: Each army withdrew to its home command.

sentences.zh: 子儀以朔方軍保河陽，斷浮橋，有詔令留守東都。

translations.literal: Ziyi held Heyang with the Shuofang Army, cut the pontoon bridge, and received an edict ordering him to remain and guard the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi held Heyang with the Shuofang Army, cut the pontoon bridge, and was ordered by edict to remain and guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 三月，以子儀為東都畿、山南東道、河南諸道行營元帥。

translations.literal: In the third month, Ziyi was made supreme commander of the field headquarters for the Eastern Capital Metropolitan Area, Shannan East Circuit, and the various circuits of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Ziyi was appointed supreme commander of the field headquarters for the Eastern Capital region, Shannan East Circuit, and the Henan circuits.

sentences.zh: 中官魚朝恩素害子儀之功，因其不振，媒孽之，尋召還京師。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yu Chao'en had long resented Ziyi's achievements; taking advantage of his setback, he slandered him, and soon Ziyi was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yu Chao'en had long resented Ziyi's achievements. Seizing on his setback, Yu slandered him, and Ziyi was soon recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天子以趙王系為天下兵馬元帥，李光弼副之，委以陜東軍事，代子儀之任。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven appointed the Prince of Zhao, Xi, supreme commander of all armies and horses, with Li Guangbi as his deputy, entrusting him with military affairs east of Shaan in place of Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Prince of Zhao Xi supreme commander of all armies, with Li Guangbi as deputy, and entrusted him with military affairs east of Shaan in Ziyi's place.

sentences.zh: 子儀雖失兵柄，乃思王室，以禍難未平，不遑寢息。

translations.literal: Though Ziyi had lost military command, he still thought of the imperial house; because the calamity was not yet ended, he had no leisure to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ziyi had lost command of the army, his thoughts remained with the throne. With the realm still in turmoil, he scarcely slept.

sentences.zh: 俄而史思明再陷河洛，朝廷旰食，復慮蕃寇逼迫京畿，三年正月，授子儀邠寧、鄜坊兩鎮節度使，仍留京師。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Siming again seized the He-Luo region; the court ate late into the evening in anxiety and again feared non-Han raiders pressing upon the capital region. In the first month of the third year, Ziyi was made military governor of the two commands of Binning and Fufang, yet he remained at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shi Siming seized the He-Luo region again. The court labored late into the evening in anxiety and again feared barbarian raids on the capital. In the first month of the third year Ziyi was made military governor of Binning and Fufang, yet he remained at court.

sentences.zh: 言事者以子儀有社稷大功，今殘孽未除，不宜置之散地，肅宗深然之。

translations.literal: Memorialists argued that Ziyi had great merit for the altars of state and that, with rebel remnants not yet eliminated, he should not be placed in an idle post; Suzong deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists argued that Ziyi had rendered great service to the dynasty and that, with rebel remnants still abroad, he should not be left idle. Suzong strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 上元元年九月，以子儀為諸道兵馬都統，管崇嗣副之，令率英武、威遠等禁軍及河西、河東諸鎮之師，取邠寧、朔方、大同、橫野，徑抵范陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Shangyuan, Ziyi was made overall commander of armies and horses of all circuits, with Guan Chongsi as deputy, and ordered to lead the imperial guard units Yingwu and Weiyuan and the armies of the Hexi and Hedong commands to take Binning, Shuofang, Datong, and Hengye and strike straight for Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Shangyuan 1 (760) Ziyi was made overall commander of all circuit armies, with Guan Chongsi as deputy, and ordered to lead the Yingwu and Weiyuan palace guards and the Hexi and Hedong commands to recover Binning, Shuofang, Datong, and Hengye and march straight on Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 詔下旬日，復為朝恩所間，事竟不行。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to set out within ten days, but again Yu Chao'en interfered, and in the end the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered departure within ten days, but Yu Chao'en interfered again and the campaign never took place.

sentences.zh: 二月，李光弼兵敗於邙山，河陽失守，魚朝恩退保陜州。

translations.literal: In the second month, Li Guangbi's army was defeated at Mount Mang, Heyang was lost, and Yu Chao'en withdrew to hold Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Guangbi was defeated at Mount Mang, Heyang fell, and Yu Chao'en withdrew to hold Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，河中軍亂，殺其帥李國貞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, the Hezhong army mutinied and killed its commander Li Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year the Hezhong army mutinied and killed its commander Li Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 時太原節度鄧景山亦為部下所殺，恐其合從連賊，朝廷憂之。

translations.literal: At that time the Taiyuan military governor Deng Jingshan was also killed by his subordinates; fearing they might join together and link with the rebels, the court was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Taiyuan military governor Deng Jingshan was killed by his own men. The court feared the mutinies might join forces and ally with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 後輩帥臣未能彈壓，勢不獲已，遂用子儀為朔方、河中、北庭、潞、儀、澤、沁等州節度行營兼興平、定國副元帥，充本管觀察處置使，進封汾陽郡王，出鎮絳州。

translations.literal: Later commanders could not suppress the unrest; the situation left no choice, and Ziyi was appointed commander of the field headquarters for the circuits of Shuofang, Hezhong, Beiting, Lu, Yi, Ze, and Qin, concurrently deputy supreme commander for Xingping and Dingguo, and commissioner for observation and disposition of his jurisdiction; he was advanced to Prince of Fenyang and went out to command from Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later commanders could not suppress the unrest, and the court had no choice. Ziyi was made commander of the field headquarters for Shuofang, Hezhong, Beiting, Lu, Yi, Ze, and Qin, concurrently deputy supreme commander for Xingping and Dingguo, and commissioner for observation and disposition of his jurisdiction. He was ennobled as Prince of Fenyang and sent out to take command from Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，子儀辭赴鎮，肅宗不豫，群臣莫有見者。

translations.literal: In the third month, Ziyi took leave to go to his command; Suzong was unwell, and none of the ministers had been received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Ziyi took leave to go to his post. Suzong was ill, and none of the ministers had been granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 子儀請曰：「老臣受命，將死於外，不見陛下，目不瞑矣。

translations.literal: Ziyi petitioned: "This old minister has received his commission and will die abroad; if I do not see Your Majesty, my eyes will not close in death."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi petitioned, "This old servant has received his commission and will die in the field. If I do not see Your Majesty, my eyes will not close in death."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃引至臥內，謂子儀曰：「河東之事，一以委卿。

translations.literal: The emperor then led him into the inner chamber and said to Ziyi: "Matters in Hedong I entrust entirely to you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then led him into the inner chamber and said, "Matters in Hedong I entrust entirely to you."

sentences.zh: 」子儀嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: Ziyi sobbed convulsively, tears streaming down.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi sobbed convulsively, tears streaming down.

sentences.zh: 賜禦馬、銀器、雜彩，別賜絹四萬疋、布五萬端以賞軍。

translations.literal: He was granted imperial horses, silver vessels, and various colored silks; separately he was granted forty thousand bolts of silk and fifty thousand bolts of cloth to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him imperial horses, silver vessels, and various colored silks, and separately awarded forty thousand bolts of silk and fifty thousand bolts of cloth to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 子儀至絳，擒其殺國貞賊首王元振數十人誅之。

translations.literal: When Ziyi reached Jiang Prefecture, he captured several dozen bandit chiefs including Wang Yuanzhen, who had killed Guozhen, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi reached Jiang Prefecture, he captured and executed several dozen rebel ringleaders, including Wang Yuanzhen, who had killed Li Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 太原辛雲京聞子儀誅元振，亦誅害景山者，由是河東諸鎮率皆奉法。

translations.literal: Xin Yunjing of Taiyuan, hearing that Ziyi had executed Yuanzhen, also executed those who had harmed Jingshan; from this the various garrisons of Hedong for the most part all obeyed the law.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yunjing of Taiyuan, learning that Ziyi had executed Yuanzhen, also put to death those who had killed Deng Jingshan. Thereafter the garrisons of Hedong for the most part all submitted to authority.

sentences.zh: 四月，代宗即位，內官程元振用事，自矜定策之功，忌嫉宿將，以子儀功高難制，巧行離間，請罷副元帥，加實封七百戶，充肅宗山陵使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Emperor Daizong ascended the throne. The inner eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen wielded power, priding himself on his merit in settling the succession and jealous of veteran generals; because Ziyi's achievements were too great to control, he craftily sowed discord, requesting that the post of deputy supreme commander be abolished, adding seven hundred taxable households to his enfeoffment, and appointing him supervisor of Emperor Suzong's mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Daizong took the throne. The eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen held power, boasting of his role in securing the succession and resenting veteran commanders. Because Ziyi's stature made him hard to control, Cheng craftily drove wedges between him and the throne, asking that his deputy marshal's post be removed, that seven hundred taxable households be added to his fief, and that he be made supervisor of Suzong's mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 子儀既謝恩，上表進肅宗所賜前後詔敕，因自陳訴曰：

translations.literal: After Ziyi had expressed his gratitude, he submitted a memorial returning the various edicts and orders previously granted by Emperor Suzong, and thereby made his own petition, saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Ziyi had thanked the emperor, he submitted a memorial returning the edicts Suzong had granted him before and after, and lodged his own complaint, saying:

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「」代宗以子儀頃同患難，收復兩京，禮之逾厚。

translations.literal: The edict replied: "" Because Daizong had recently shared hardships with Ziyi and Ziyi had recovered the two capitals, he treated him with ever greater honor.
translations.idiomatic: The edict made no formal reply. Because Daizong had lately endured hardship alongside Ziyi and because Ziyi had recovered the two capitals, the emperor treated him with ever greater honor.

sentences.zh: 時史朝義尚據洛陽，元帥雍王率師進討，代宗欲以子儀副之，而魚朝恩、程元振亂政，殺裴茂、來瑱，子儀既為所間，其事遂寢，乃留京師。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Chaoyi still held Luoyang; the supreme commander, the Prince of Yong, led an army forward to attack him. Daizong wished to make Ziyi his deputy, but Yu Chao'en and Cheng Yuanzhen misgoverned, killing Pei Mao and Lai Tian; Ziyi having been alienated by them, the matter was shelved, and he remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shi Chaoyi still held Luoyang, and the Prince of Yong, as supreme commander, marched to attack him. Daizong wished to appoint Ziyi as his deputy, but Yu Chao'en and Cheng Yuanzhen were corrupting the government and had Pei Mao and Lai Tian killed. Ziyi had been turned against, the plan came to nothing, and he remained at court.

sentences.zh: 俄而梁崇義據襄陽叛，僕固懷恩阻兵於汾州，引回紇、吐蕃之眾入寇河西。

translations.literal: Before long Liang Chongyi seized Xiangyang and rebelled; Pugu Huaien held troops in defiance at Fen Prefecture and led Uyghur and Tibetan forces to raid Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Liang Chongyi seized Xiangyang and rebelled, while Pugu Huaien defied the court with troops at Fen Prefecture and brought Uyghur and Tibetan forces to raid Hexi.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，吐蕃陷涇州，虜刺史高暉，暉遂與蕃軍為鄉導，引賊深入京畿，掠奉天、武功，濟渭而南，緣山而東。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year the Tibetans captured Jing Prefecture and captured the prefect Gao Hui; Hui then served the Tibetan army as a local guide, leading the enemy deep into the capital region, plundering Fengtian and Wugong, crossing the Wei River southward and advancing eastward along the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the following year the Tibetans took Jing Prefecture and captured its prefect, Gao Hui. Hui then guided the Tibetan army inland, leading the enemy deep into the capital region. They plundered Fengtian and Wugong, crossed the Wei southward, and marched east along the foothills.

sentences.zh: 渭北行營兵馬使呂日將逆戰於盩厔，自辰至酉，殺蕃軍數千，然其徒多殞。

translations.literal: Lu Rijiang, army-and-horse commissioner of the Weibei field headquarters, met them in battle at Zhouzhi; from the hour chen to the hour you he killed several thousand Tibetan troops, yet many of his own men also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rijiang, cavalry commander of the Weibei field headquarters, met the invaders at Zhouzhi. From morning until evening he killed several thousand Tibetans, but many of his own men fell as well.

sentences.zh: 賊將逼京師，君上計無所出，遽詔子儀為關內副元帥，出鎮咸陽。

translations.literal: As the enemy generals pressed upon the capital, the sovereign could devise no plan; he urgently appointed Ziyi deputy supreme commander of Guannei and sent him out to take command at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: With enemy generals closing on the capital and the emperor at a loss, an urgent edict made Ziyi deputy supreme commander of Guannei and sent him out to hold Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 子儀自相州不利，李光弼代掌兵柄，及征還朝廷，部曲散去。

translations.literal: Since Ziyi had met with misfortune at Xiang Prefecture, Li Guangbi had replaced him in command of the army; when he was recalled to court, his personal followers dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since his setback at Xiang Prefecture, when Li Guangbi had taken over command, Ziyi's retainers had scattered once he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 及是承詔，部下唯二十騎，強取民家畜產以助軍。

translations.literal: When he received this edict, his subordinates numbered only twenty horsemen; he forcibly seized livestock from civilian households to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: When he answered this summons, only twenty horsemen remained under his command. He forcibly requisitioned livestock from local households to support the army.

sentences.zh: 至咸陽，蕃軍已過渭水。

translations.literal: When he reached Xianyang, the Tibetan army had already crossed the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Xianyang, the Tibetan army had already crossed the Wei.

sentences.zh: 其日，天子避狄幸陜州。

translations.literal: That day the Son of Heaven fled the barbarians to Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the emperor fled the barbarian advance to Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子儀聞上避狄，雪涕還京，至則車駕已發。

translations.literal: When Ziyi heard that the emperor had fled the barbarians, he wiped away tears and returned to the capital; when he arrived, the imperial carriage had already departed.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the emperor had fled, Ziyi wiped away his tears and hurried back to the capital, but by the time he arrived the imperial procession was already gone.

sentences.zh: 射生將王獻忠從駕，沿路遂以四百騎叛，仍逼豐王已下十王欲投於賊。

translations.literal: The imperial hunt guard Wang Xianzhong accompanied the carriage; along the route he then rebelled with four hundred horsemen and even coerced the ten princes below the Prince of Feng to defect to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial hunt guard Wang Xianzhong rode with the procession, but along the way he rebelled with four hundred horsemen and forced ten princes, beginning with the Prince of Feng, toward defection to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 子儀入開遠門，遇之，詰豐王等所向，遂護送行在。

translations.literal: Ziyi entered Kaiyuan Gate, encountered them, questioned the Prince of Feng and the others as to where they were going, and then escorted and sent off the imperial presence.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi entered Kaiyuan Gate, intercepted them, demanded to know where the Prince of Feng and the others were headed, and then escorted the imperial presence on its way.

sentences.zh: 子儀以三千騎傍南山，至商州，得武關防兵及六軍散卒四千人，招輯亡逸，其軍漸振。

translations.literal: Ziyi, with three thousand horsemen along the southern mountains, reached Shang Prefecture; there he obtained the Wuguan garrison troops and four thousand scattered soldiers of the Six Armies, gathered fugitives, and his army gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi led three thousand horsemen along the southern slopes to Shang Prefecture, where he gathered the Wuguan garrison and four thousand scattered soldiers from the Six Armies, rallied the fugitives, and gradually restored his force.

sentences.zh: 蕃犯京城，得故邠王守禮子廣武王承宏，立帝號，假署百官。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans violated the capital, they obtained Cheng Hong, Prince of Guangwu, son of the former Prince of Bin Li Shouli; they established an imperial title and provisionally appointed the full roster of officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans entered the capital, they found Cheng Hong, Prince of Guangwu, son of the former Prince of Bin, Li Shouli. They set up an imperial regime and provisionally appointed a full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 子儀遣六軍兵馬使張知節、烏崇福、羽林軍使長孫全緒等將兵萬人為前鋒，營於韓公堆，盛張旗幟，鼓鞞震山谷。

translations.literal: Ziyi dispatched the Six Armies cavalry commissioners Zhang Zhijie and Wu Chongfu, the Imperial Guard commander Zhangsun Quanxu, and others to lead ten thousand men as the vanguard; they encamped at Han Gongdui, greatly displayed banners and flags, and their drums shook the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi sent the Six Armies cavalry commissioners Zhang Zhijie and Wu Chongfu, the Imperial Guard commander Zhangsun Quanxu, and others at the head of ten thousand men. They encamped at Han Gongdui, raised a great show of banners, and beat drums that shook the valleys.

sentences.zh: 全緒遣禁軍舊將王甫入長安，陰結少年豪俠以為內應，一日，齊擊鼓於朱雀街，蕃軍惶駭而去。

translations.literal: Quanxu sent the former Imperial Guard general Wang Fu into Chang'an to secretly ally with young gallant men as an inner response; one day they beat drums together in Zhuque Street, and the Tibetan army fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Quanxu sent the former Imperial Guard officer Wang Fu into Chang'an to secretly enlist young bravos as inside allies. One day they sounded drums together in Zhuque Street, and the Tibetan army fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 大將李忠義先屯兵苑中，渭北節度使王仲升守朝堂。

translations.literal: The grand general Li Zhongyi first encamped in the imperial park, and Weibei military governor Wang Zhongsheng guarded the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Grand general Li Zhongyi first encamped in the imperial park, while Weibei military governor Wang Zhongsheng held the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 子儀以大軍續進，至浐西。

translations.literal: Ziyi continued advancing with the main army and reached the west of the Chan River.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi pressed forward with the main army as far as the west bank of the Chan River.

sentences.zh: 射生將王撫自署為京兆尹，聚兵二千人，擾亂京城，子儀召撫殺之。

translations.literal: The imperial hunt guard Wang Fu self-appointed himself Jingzhao Intendant, gathered two thousand troops, and disturbed the capital; Ziyi summoned Fu and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial hunt guard Wang Fu declared himself Jingzhao intendant, raised two thousand men, and threw the capital into disorder. Ziyi summoned him and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 詔子儀權京城留守。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ziyi provisional Protector of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Ziyi provisional protector of the capital.

sentences.zh: 自西蕃入寇，車駕東幸，天下皆咎程元振，諫官屢論之。

translations.literal: Since the Western barbarians had invaded and the imperial carriage had gone east, all under Heaven blamed Cheng Yuanzhen, and remonstrating officials repeatedly criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: After the western barbarians invaded and the emperor fled east, the whole empire blamed Cheng Yuanzhen, and censors repeatedly denounced him.

sentences.zh: 元振懼，又以子儀復立功，不欲天子還京，勸帝且都洛陽以避蕃冠，代宗然之，下詔有日。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen grew afraid; moreover, because Ziyi had again won merit, he did not wish the Son of Heaven to return to the capital and advised the emperor to establish the court temporarily at Luoyang to avoid the Tibetan invaders. Daizong agreed, and an edict was to be issued on a set day.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen was afraid, and because Ziyi had distinguished himself again he did not want the emperor to return to Chang'an. He urged Daizong to move the court temporarily to Luoyang to escape the Tibetans. Daizong agreed, and an edict was set to be issued.

sentences.zh: 子儀聞之，因兵部侍郎張重光宣慰回，附章論奏曰：

translations.literal: When Ziyi heard of this, as Vice Director of the Ministry of War Zhang Chongguang returned from his consolation mission, he attached a memorial arguing his case, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi heard of this, he sent a memorial with Zhang Chongguang, vice director of the Ministry of War, as the latter returned from a consolation tour, arguing against the move. He wrote:

sentences.zh: 代宗省表，垂泣謂左右曰：「子儀用心，真社稷臣也。

translations.literal: Daizong read the memorial and, weeping, told those around him: "Ziyi's devotion makes him a true minister of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong read the memorial and, weeping, told those around him, "In his loyalty Ziyi is a true pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 可亟還京師。

translations.literal: We may return to the capital at once.
translations.idiomatic: We should return to the capital at once.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，車駕自陜還宮，子儀伏地請罪，帝駐車勞之曰：「朕用卿不早，故及於此。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the imperial carriage returned from Shan Prefecture to the palace; Ziyi prostrated himself and asked to be punished. The emperor stopped his carriage and consoled him, saying: "I did not employ you soon enough, and hence we came to this.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor returned from Shan Prefecture to the palace. Ziyi prostrated himself and asked to be punished. The emperor halted his carriage and comforted him, saying, "I did not use you soon enough, and that is why this happened.

sentences.zh: 」乃賜鐵券，圖形淩煙閣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted an iron certificate and had his likeness placed in Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted Ziyi an iron certificate of immunity and had his portrait placed in Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 是時，河北副元帥僕固懷恩方頓軍汾州，掠并、汾諸縣以為己邑。

translations.literal: At this time the Hebei deputy supreme commander Pugu Huaien was encamped at Fen Prefecture, plundering the counties of Bing and Fen and treating them as his own territory.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Pugu Huaien, deputy supreme commander of Hebei, was encamped at Fen Prefecture, plundering the counties of Bing and Fen and treating them as his private domain.

sentences.zh: 乃以子儀兼關內河東副元帥、河中節度觀察使，出鎮河中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ziyi was made concurrently deputy supreme commander of Guannei and Hedong and military governor and observation commissioner of Hezhong, and sent out to take command at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: The court then made Ziyi concurrently deputy supreme commander of Guannei and Hedong and military governor and observation commissioner of Hezhong, and sent him out to command from there.

sentences.zh: 蕃戎既退，僕固懷恩部下離散。

translations.literal: Once the barbarians of the west had withdrawn, the subordinates of Pugu Huaien dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the western barbarians had withdrawn, Pugu Huaien's followers scattered.

sentences.zh: 是月，懷恩子瑒主兵榆次，為帳下將張惟嶽所殺，傳首京師。

translations.literal: That month Huaien's son Yang commanded troops at Yuci and was killed by his tent officer Zhang Weiyue; his head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That month Huaien's son Yang held troops at Yuci and was killed by his officer Zhang Weiyue; his head was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽以瑒之眾歸於子儀，懷恩懼，棄其母而走靈州。

translations.literal: Weiyue brought Yang's troops to submit to Ziyi; Huaien was afraid, abandoned his mother, and fled to Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue brought Yang's troops over to Ziyi. Huaien, terrified, abandoned his mother and fled to Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年九月，以子儀守太尉，充北道邠寧、涇原、河西已東通和蕃及朔方招撫觀察使，其關內河東副元帥、中書令如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the following year Ziyi was appointed Grand Preceptor and made Northern Circuit pacification and observation commissioner for Binning, Jingyuan, and Hexi eastward, for communicating with and harmonizing the Tibetans, and for Shuofang; his posts as deputy supreme commander of Guannei and Hedong and as Grand Councilor remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the following year Ziyi was made Grand Preceptor and appointed northern-circuit pacification and observation commissioner over Binning, Jingyuan, Hexi eastward, and Shuofang, charged with managing relations with the Tibetans. His posts as deputy supreme commander of Guannei and Hedong and as grand councilor remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 子儀以懷恩未誅，不宜讓使，堅辭太尉，曰：「太尉職雄任重，竊憂非據，輒敢上聞。

translations.literal: Because Huaien had not yet been executed, Ziyi held that it was not fitting to accept the commission; he firmly declined the Grand Preceptor's post, saying: "The office of Grand Preceptor is lofty and its burden heavy; I privately fear I am not equal to the post and venture to report this to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huaien had not yet been brought to justice, Ziyi held that he ought not accept the appointment. He firmly declined the Grand Preceptor's post, saying, "The Grand Preceptor's office is exalted and its burden heavy. I fear I am unworthy of it and venture to lay this before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 伏奉詔書，未允誠懇。

translations.literal: Having received the imperial edict in submission, my sincere request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: I have received Your Majesty's edict, yet my sincere request has not been granted.

sentences.zh: 臣疇昔之分，早知止足，今茲累請，竊懼滿盈。

translations.literal: Your subject's allotted portion from of old—I early knew when to stop; now, with these repeated requests, I privately fear overflowing fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has long known the limits of his proper share and when to stop. These repeated petitions come only from my fear of excess.

sentences.zh: 義實由衷，事非矯飾，志之所至，敢不盡言。

translations.literal: The righteousness is truly from the heart; the matter is not feigned ornament. Where my will reaches, how dare I not speak fully?
translations.idiomatic: This is sincere conviction, not pretense. Where my heart leads, how can I fail to speak plainly?

sentences.zh: 自兵亂已來，紀綱浸壞，時多躁競，俗少廉隅。

translations.literal: Since the military chaos began, regulations have gradually deteriorated; the age has much rash competition, and custom has little integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, discipline has steadily decayed. The age is full of reckless ambition, and integrity has grown rare.

sentences.zh: 德薄而位尊，功微而賞厚，實繁有眾，不可殫論。

translations.literal: Virtue is thin yet position is eminent; merit is slight yet reward is generous—such cases are indeed many and cannot be exhaustively discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Men of slight virtue hold lofty rank; men of slight merit receive lavish reward. Such cases are countless and cannot all be discussed.

sentences.zh: 臣每見之，深以為念。

translations.literal: Whenever your subject sees this, he deeply takes it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I see this, it weighs heavily on my mind.

sentences.zh: 昔范宣子讓，其下皆讓，欒騕為汰，不敢違也。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Fan Xuanzi yielded, those beneath all yielded; though Luan Yan was dissolute, he did not dare defy it.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when Fan Xuanzi yielded office, all beneath him yielded as well. Even Luan Yan, for all his excess, did not dare break that example.

sentences.zh: 臣誠薄劣，竊慕古人，務欲以身率先，大變浮俗，是用勤勤懇懇，願罷此官，庶禮讓興行，由臣而致也。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly base and inferior, yet privately admires the ancients and strives to lead by personal example and greatly transform floating custom; therefore I am diligent and earnest in wishing to resign this office, hoping that courtesy and yielding may arise and be achieved through me.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of little worth, yet I admire the ancients and wish to lead by example and change these shallow ways. That is why I earnestly beg to be relieved of this office, so that courtesy and restraint may be restored through my act.

sentences.zh: 臣位為上相，爵為真王，參啟沃之謀，受腹心之寄，恩榮已極，功業已成，尋合乞骸，保全餘齒。

translations.literal: Your subject's rank is chief minister and his ennoblement is that of a full prince; I participate in counsel of utmost trust and have received the heart-and-belly entrustment. Grace and glory have already reached their limit, and my achievements are already complete—it is fitting soon to request retirement and preserve my remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: I stand as chief minister and hold the rank of a full prince. I share in the deepest counsel of state and bear the emperor's innermost trust. Honor has already reached its height, and my work is done. It is time to ask leave to retire and preserve what years remain to me.

sentences.zh: 但以冠仇在近，家國未安，臣子之心，不敢寧處。

translations.literal: Only because the crowned enemy is near at hand, the state and family are not yet secure—the heart of a subject and minister dares not dwell in ease.
translations.idiomatic: It is only that our mortal foe still presses close, the realm and house are not yet at peace, and the heart of a loyal subject cannot rest easy.

sentences.zh: 茍西戎即敘，懷恩就擒，疇昔官爵，誓無所受，必當追蹤范蠡，繼跡留侯。

translations.literal: If the Western Rong are at once pacified and Huai'en is captured and taken, the official ranks of former days I swear I shall not accept; I shall surely follow in the tracks of Fan Li and continue in the footsteps of the Marquis of Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Should the western tribes be brought to order and Huai'en taken prisoner, I swear I will accept none of the honors I once held. I mean to retire as Fan Li did, and walk the path of the Marquis of Liu.

sentences.zh: 臣之鄙懷，切在於此。

translations.literal: Your subject's humble wish is urgently set upon this.
translations.idiomatic: This, and nothing else, is the humble wish I hold in my heart.

sentences.zh: 」優詔不許。

translations.literal: An excellent edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict refusing his request.

sentences.zh: 子儀見上，感泣懇讓，乃止。

translations.literal: Ziyi had an audience with the emperor, wept in gratitude and earnestly declined, and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi went before the throne, wept as he pleaded to be released from the honor, and at last desisted.

sentences.zh: 十月，僕固懷恩引吐蕃、回紇、党項數十萬南下，京師大恐，子儀出鎮奉天。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Pugu Huai'en led several hundred thousand Tibetans, Uyghurs, and Tanguts southward; the capital was greatly terrified, and Ziyi went out to command at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Pugu Huai'en marched south at the head of several hundred thousand Tibetans, Uyghurs, and Tangut warriors. Terror seized the capital, and Ziyi rode out to take command at Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 帝召子儀問禦戎之計，子儀曰：「以臣所見，懷恩無能為也。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Ziyi to ask about plans for repelling the barbarians. Ziyi said: "In your subject's view, Huai'en will not be able to accomplish anything."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Ziyi in to ask how the invaders might be repelled. Ziyi answered, "As I see it, Huai'en can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 」帝問其故，對曰：「懷恩雖稱驍勇，素失士心，今所以能為亂者，引思歸之人耳。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason. He replied: "Although Huai'en is called brave and fierce, he has long lost the hearts of his soldiers; what enables him to make trouble now is only that he is leading men who long to return home."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked why, he replied, "Huai'en may have a name for valor, but he lost his men's loyalty long ago. All that lets him raise rebellion is that he is dragging along troops who only want to go home."

sentences.zh: 懷恩本臣偏將，其下皆臣之部曲，臣恩信嘗及之，今臣為大將，必不忍以鋒刃相向，以此知其無能為也。

translations.literal: Huai'en was originally your subject's junior general; those beneath him were all your subject's personal troops. Your subject's grace and trust once reached them. Now that your subject is the grand general, they surely cannot bear to turn blades against me—by this I know he will not be able to accomplish anything.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was once my subordinate, and his men were my own troops. They knew my kindness and trust. Now that I command the army, they will not willingly cross swords with me. That is how I know he can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 」虜寇邠州，子儀在涇陽，子儀令長男朔方兵馬使曜率師援之，與邠寧節度使白孝德閉城拒守。

translations.literal: The barbarians raided Bin Prefecture. Ziyi was at Jingyang. Ziyi ordered his eldest son, the Shuofang army-and-horse commissioner Yao, to lead troops to reinforce it; together with the Binning military governor Bai Xiaode, they closed the city and held fast in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy struck Bin Prefecture while Ziyi was at Jingyang. He sent his eldest son Guo Yao, military commissioner of Shuofang, to relieve the city. With Bai Xiaode, military governor of Binning, they shut the gates and stood firm.

sentences.zh: 懷恩前鋒至奉天，近城挑戰，諸將請擊之，子儀止之曰：「夫客兵深入，利在速戰，不可爭鋒。

translations.literal: Huai'en's vanguard reached Fengtian, drew near the city, and offered battle. The generals requested to attack, but Ziyi stopped them, saying: "An invading army that has penetrated deep gains advantage in quick battle—one must not contend at the spearpoint.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's advance guard reached Fengtian and challenged the walls. The officers wanted to strike, but Ziyi forbade it. "An enemy army deep in hostile country wants a quick fight," he said. "We must not meet them blade to blade.

sentences.zh: 彼皆吾之部曲，緩之自當攜貳；

translations.literal: They are all my former troops; if we take it slowly, they will naturally become divided in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Those men were once mine. Give them time, and they will split among themselves.

sentences.zh: 若迫之，是速其戰，戰則勝負未可知。

translations.literal: If we press them, we will hasten their battle; once they fight, victory and defeat cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Drive them hard and you force the battle—and then who can say who will win?

sentences.zh: 敢言戰者斬！

translations.literal: Whoever dares speak of fighting shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Let any man who dares speak of giving battle lose his head!

sentences.zh: 」堅壁待之，果不戰而退。

translations.literal: They fortified the walls and waited; sure enough, without fighting they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They held behind strong walls and waited. In the end the enemy withdrew without a fight.

sentences.zh: 子儀自涇陽入朝，帝御安福門待之，命子儀樓上行朝見之禮，宴賜隆厚。

translations.literal: Ziyi entered court from Jingyang. The emperor awaited him at Anfu Gate, ordered Ziyi to perform the court-audience rite from atop the gate tower, and bestowed a banquet with lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi came to court from Jingyang. The emperor received him at Anfu Gate, had him perform the audience ceremony from the gate tower, and honored him with a feast and rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以子儀為尚書令，上表懇辭曰：「臣以薄劣，素乏行能，逢時擾攘，猥蒙驅策，內參朝政，外總兵權。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Ziyi was made Director of the Imperial Secretariat. He submitted a memorial earnestly declining: "Your subject, by virtue of my thin merit and inferior quality, has always lacked conduct and ability. Encountering a troubled age, I have undeservedly received driving command. Within I participate in court governance; without I hold overall military authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Ziyi was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat. He memorialized the throne in earnest refusal: "I am a man of little talent and poor merit. In these turbulent times I have undeservedly been pressed into service, sharing in court policy within and commanding armies without.

sentences.zh: 上不能翼戴三光，下不能糾逖群慝，功微賞厚，任重恩深，覆餗之憂，實盈寤寐。

translations.literal: Above I cannot uphold the Three Luminaries; below I cannot rectify distant evils. My merit is slight yet my rewards are heavy; my burdens are great yet your grace is deep. The fear of overturning the pot truly fills my waking and sleeping hours.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot worthily serve heaven, earth, and the sovereign above, nor put down wickedness far and near below. My deeds are small while your gifts are great; my burden is heavy while your kindness runs deep. Night and day I live in dread of failing you.

sentences.zh: 臣昨所以固辭太尉，乞保餘年，殊私曲臨，遂見矜許。

translations.literal: Yesterday your subject, for this reason, firmly declined the post of Grand Commandant, begging to preserve my remaining years. Your extraordinary private kindness bent down to me, and I was thus granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday I firmly refused the Grand Commandant's seal and begged to keep what years remain to me. Your Majesty's gracious indulgence bent to my wish, and you were pleased to allow it.

sentences.zh: 竊謂陛下已知其願，深察其心，豈意未歷旬時，復延寵命。

translations.literal: I privately supposed Your Majesty already knew my wish and had deeply discerned my heart. How could I have expected that, before ten days had passed, you would again extend a favoring appointment?
translations.idiomatic: I had thought Your Majesty understood my wish and saw my heart clearly. I never imagined that in less than ten days you would honor me with a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 以臣褊淺，又寡智謀，安可謬職南宮，當茲大任？

translations.literal: Given my narrowness and shallowness, and my lack of wisdom and strategy, how could I wrongly occupy the Southern Palace post and bear this great responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: I am narrow-minded, shallow, and lacking in counsel. How can such a man rightly fill the office of the Secretariat and shoulder so great a charge?

sentences.zh: 況太宗昔居籓邸，嘗踐此官，累聖相承，曠而不置。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Taizong formerly resided in the princely residence, he once held this office. Successive sages have inherited it, and the post has long gone unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when Emperor Taizong still lived in the princely residence he once held this office. Since then successive sage emperors have kept it vacant.

sentences.zh: 皇太子為雍王之日，陛下以其總兵薄伐，平定關東，飲至策勛，再有斯授。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was Prince of Yong, Your Majesty, because he had marshaled troops on a punitive expedition and pacified the eastern passes, at the ceremony of drinking to victory and recording merits, again received this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince was still Prince of Yong, Your Majesty gave him this post after he took command of a punitive campaign, pacified the eastern passes, and was honored at the victory feast for his deeds.

sentences.zh: 豈臣末職，敢亂大倫？

translations.literal: How could one of lowly rank like your subject dare disrupt the great order?
translations.idiomatic: How could a man of my humble station dare disturb so august a precedent?

sentences.zh: 德薄位尊，難逃天子之責；

translations.literal: My virtue is thin yet my position is exalted—hard to escape the Son of Heaven's reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue too slight for so high a rank cannot escape the judgment of heaven's son.

sentences.zh: 負乘致冠，復速神明之誅。

translations.literal: Like a small beast bearing too heavy a load, I would again hasten divine punishment.
translations.idiomatic: To take on more than my strength can bear would only invite heaven's wrath upon me.

sentences.zh: 伏乞天慈，俯停新命。

translations.literal: I humbly beg Heaven's mercy to bend and halt this new appointment.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty, in your heavenly kindness, to withdraw this new command.

sentences.zh: 」答詔不允。

translations.literal: The reply edict did not accede.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's written reply refused to grant his request.

sentences.zh: 翌日，敕所司令子儀於尚書省視事。

translations.literal: The next day, an edict ordered the responsible offices to have Ziyi assume duties at the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following day an edict commanded the relevant offices to install Ziyi at the Secretariat to begin his duties.

sentences.zh: 詔宰相百僚送上，遣射生五百騎執戟翼從，自朝堂至省，賜教坊樂。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the chancellors and the hundred officials to escort him up; five hundred mounted archers bearing halberds were dispatched to flank and follow him from the court hall to the Secretariat, and music from the Music Bureau was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the chief ministers and all officials to escort him in procession. Five hundred mounted archers with halberds rode in attendance from the hall of audience to the Secretariat, and musicians from the imperial Music Bureau were sent to honor the occasion.

sentences.zh: 子儀不受，復上表曰：

translations.literal: Ziyi did not accept, and again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi still refused the honor and submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 手詔答曰：「」遣內侍魚朝恩傳詔，賜美人盧氏等六人、從者八人，並車服、帷帳、床蓐、珍玩之具。

translations.literal: An imperial handwritten edict replied: "" The eunuch Yu Chao'en was dispatched to convey the edict, granting the beauties including Lady Lu—six persons in all—eight attendants, together with carriages, robes, curtains, bedding, and objects of precious play.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a personal edict. He sent the eunuch Yu Chao'en to deliver it, along with six concubines including Lady Lu, eight attendants, and a full provision of carriages, robes, curtains, bedding, and fine treasures.

sentences.zh: 時蕃虜屢寇京畿，倚蒲、陜為內地，常以重兵鎮之。

translations.literal: At this time the barbarian raiders repeatedly attacked the capital region; relying on Pu and Shaan as inner territory, the court constantly stationed heavy troops there to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the frontier tribes raided the capital region again and again. The court treated Pu and Shaan as inner lands and kept large garrisons there.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年五月，以子儀都統河南道節度行營，出鎮河中。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongtai, Ziyi was made overall commander of the Henan Circuit defense mobile headquarters and went out to command at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongtai, Ziyi was appointed supreme commander of the Henan defense headquarters and took up his post at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 八月，僕固懷恩誘吐蕃、回紇、党項、羌、渾、奴剌，山賊任敷、鄭庭、郝德、劉開元等三十餘萬南下，先發數萬人掠同州，期自華陰趨藍田，以扼南路，懷恩率重兵繼其後。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Pugu Huai'en incited Tibet, Uyghur, Tangut, Qiang, Hun, and Nula tribes, together with mountain bandits Ren Fu, Zheng Ting, Hao De, Liu Kaiyuan, and others—over three hundred thousand in all—to march south. He first sent tens of thousands to plunder Tong Prefecture, intending to advance from Huayin toward Lantian to choke the southern route; Huai'en followed with heavy troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Pugu Huai'en stirred up Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tanguts, Qiang, Hun, and Nula, along with mountain rebels Ren Fu, Zheng Ting, Hao De, Liu Kaiyuan, and others—more than three hundred thousand men in all—to march south.
